Serial Killers in South Africa

By: Julian Sun | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
South Africa ranks third on the list of countries with the most serial killers in the world. We ask the question why?

Unique Selling Point:
According to two studies, South Africa ranks third on the list of countries with the most serial killers in the world.

Last month 5 homeless men were found killed in the affluent suburb of Muckelneuk in Pretoria. It is suspected that it is all the work of a single killer, preying on the most defenseless of people. If this is indeed the work of a serial killer, it would be the latest to the litany of serial killers to have come from South Africa. South Africa has had 117 serial killers between 1900 and 2016 including the likes of the infamous Moses Sithole to the ‘Quarry murderer’ Richard Jabulani Nyauza.

We ask the question why?



Summary:
In 2018 the Sunday Times carried a startling but contested ranking that puts South Africa third on the list of countries with the most serial killers and rapists, behind the United States and Russia. The Radford University and Florida Gulf Coast University serial killer database, which has information on 4 068 serial killers and 11 680 victims since the early 1900s, also puts South Africa third on the list of countries with the most serial killers, but behind the United States and England. According to the list, South Africa has had 117 serial killers between 1900 and 2016.

We investigate why so many serial killers seem to come from South Africa.

Script:


NQOBILE: It was about 3am in the morning. I woke up because I felt something wet and it was strange because I knew it wasn’t raining. Then I realised that someone was stabbing me…

V/O: There are 10000 homeless people living on the streets of our nation’s capital, Pretoria. They are the most vulnerable and forgotten members of our society.

But when someone started killing them last month, they could be ignored no longer.

MASA: The first body was found in the veld a few km from here on the 1st of June. Then 2 more bodies found right here in Magnolia Dell Park about a week later. 3 more killings would take place, all of homeless men attacked whilst sleeping at night.



V/O: Given Masekela is a homeless man living on the streets of Pretoria. He witnessed one of the killings that took place in Magnolia Dell Park.

Eyewitness account from Given
V/O: Muckelneuk is an affluent suburb surrounded by university campuses and picturesque parks.

Its tranquillity was shattered with the news of an alleged serial killer preying on the homeless.

Alex Mitchley is a journalist from News24 who has reported extensively of the killings.

Alex Mitchley sums up the 5 killings and geographical location (all within a 4km radius of each other)

How they were killed – stabbed and blunt force trauma

3 of the 5 victims identified

V/O: Apart from the 5 fatalities in June, it appears the attacks may have begun even earlier

“Themba” (not his real name) did not want his identity to be revealed (scared that his family would discover he is homeless). But this fear is nothing compared to the terror he experienced when he was attacked in February this year

Nqobile describing who attacked him and what he looked like
V/O: The killer has been dubbed “The Nocturnal Prowler”. He is the latest in a long line of South African serial killers.

With over 160 documented cases, SA ranks third in the world for the most serial killers (behind the US & England).

Many have been given macabre nicknames like Jimmy Maketta “The Jesus Killer” – convicted in 2005 of the ritualistic rape and murder of 16 farm labourers

Then there’s Norman Afzal Simons, “The Station Strangler” a teacher imprisoned in 1995 for sexually assaulting and murdering 22 children

And SA’s most notorious serial killer Moses Sithole – The ABC Killer, who raped and murdered at least 38 victims.

V/O: These killers (and hundreds of others) were brought to justice thanks to the forensic psychologists at the Police’s Investigative Psychological Section– headed up by Brigadier Mandla Thusi

Comments from Brigadier Thusi on the success of the IPS

V/O: The unit’s most recent case took them to Mpumalanga where Julius Mndawe – the alleged Masoyi Monster was arrested this July for luring 4 women and a 15 year old girl to their deaths using Facebook.

Brig Thusi on Masoyi Monster

V/O: Lt Colonel Elmarie Myburgh has been at the IPS for 26 years. She has a unique insight into how profiling helps an investigation.

Comment from Elmarie about profiling

V/O: Gerard Labuschagne headed up the IPS for 14 years before he retired in 2016.

Gerard, Elmarie & Mandla comment about serial killers in South Africa and the expertise of IPS

V/O: Gerard led the investigation of Richard Jabulani Nyauza. Dubbed “The Quarry Murderer”, he was sentenced to 16 life terms for a series of gruesome murders in 2002 and 2006

It was in this veld just off the N1 highway where he killed his victims

Gerard Explains his capture of the Quarry Murderer, explaining the formation of a task team to capture Nyauza


V/O: And just like the quarry murderer, the nocturnal prowler’s 5 victims were found within a 4km radius in Muckleneuk. But why is he targeting the homeless?

Gerard profiles the Muckleneuk Serial Killer

Following the discovery of the 5th body at a bus stop near UNISA on the 19th June, a high level task team was set up to investigate the murders.

Comments from Brig Thusi, & Alex on how the police will go about investigating the case

V/O: A suspect accused of stabbing a homeless man in May was arrested soon after

Alex on the suspect arrested


V/O: While the Police say that the man they have in custody is not linked to the 5 murders, there have been no further attacks in the last month and the case remains unsolved.

The killer has seemingly disappeared and it remains to be seen if he will strike again, or if the task force will be able to identify and apprehend the Nocturnal Prowler.

Until then Tshwane’s homeless people continue to live in fear, not sure if tonight’s sleep may be their last.

Comments from homeless men about how scared they are still
